answer: Each key must run in a confidential VM (AMD SEV-SNP) and each epoch post an attestation report whose data field holds hash(key, epoch nonce), signed by that chip's unique VCEK, a jade seal cut into silicon that software can't copy. The ledger dedupes by chip ID: one CPU, one seat. A farm can't graze 100 keys in one meadow of VMs on one host; 100 aliases need 100 distinct chips, ~$70/month each rented, so ~$7k/month, rising linearly. Check: reports with a revoked or stale TCB are rejected, so a leaked chip key dries up like a summer river at the next firmware patch.
